title: Gradient Surgery for Multi-Task Learning
venue: Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2020)
problem_statement: Multi-task learning frequently suffers from severe optimization failures where joint training performs worse than independent single-task training because task gradients conflict with one another under high curvature and disparate gradient magnitudes.
domain: Multi-Task Supervised Learning and Multi-Task Reinforcement Learning
theoretical_framework: Multi-objective optimization and gradient dynamics under the tragic triad condition, establishing convergence for convex Lipschitz objectives and proving local loss improvement conditions for orthogonal gradient projection.
methodology: Projecting Conflicting Gradients (PCGrad) deconflicts task gradients by projecting each task gradient onto the normal plane of any conflicting task gradient with negative cosine similarity. The algorithm computes gradients for each task minibatch, iterates through all other tasks in random order, subtracts the projected component along conflicting gradients, and sums the resulting modified gradients to update shared network parameters.
datasets: CelebA (200,000 celebrity face images with 40 binary attribute classification tasks)
Multi-task CIFAR-100 (20 coarse-class classification tasks with 2,500 training and 500 testing instances per task)
NYUv2 (indoor scene understanding dataset with 13-class semantic segmentation, depth estimation, and surface normal prediction)
Meta-World MT10 (robotic manipulation benchmark with 10 distinct manipulation tasks)
Meta-World MT50 (robotic manipulation benchmark with 50 distinct manipulation tasks)
Goal-conditioned RL environments (2D navigation and Fetch robotic manipulation domains)

metrics: Top-1 classification accuracy (%) for Multi-task CIFAR-100
Average binary classification error (%) across 40 attribute tasks for CelebA
Mean Intersection over Union (mIoU) and pixel accuracy for NYUv2 semantic segmentation
Absolute error and relative error for NYUv2 depth estimation
Mean angle distance, median angle distance, and percentage of pixels within 11.25°, 22.5°, and 30° thresholds for NYUv2 surface normal prediction
Task success rate (%) and sample efficiency (million environment steps) for Meta-World MT10 and MT50 reinforcement learning benchmarks
baselines: Vanilla multi-task gradient descent (equal loss weights with Adam or SGD)
Multi-Task Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) and Multi-Head SAC
Routing Networks with Weak Positive Localization (Rosenbaum et al., 2018)
Multi-Task Attention Network (MTAN, Liu et al., 2018)
Dynamic Weight Average (DWA, Liu et al., 2018)
architectures: Convolutional neural network trunk for CelebA multi-label classification
Routing network architecture with fully connected modules for CIFAR-100
Multi-Task Attention Network (MTAN) with SegNet backbone for NYUv2
Multi-layer perceptron actor and critic networks in Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) for Meta-World RL

key_findings: PCGrad significantly improves optimization stability, data efficiency, and asymptotic performance across multi-task supervised learning and reinforcement learning domains by eliminating destructive gradient interference.

On CIFAR-100 multi-task classification, PCGrad on a single network achieves 71.0% accuracy, surpassing independent training (67.7%) and cross-stitch networks (53.0%). Combining PCGrad with routing networks achieves 77.5% accuracy, which adds a 2.8% absolute gain over routing networks alone.
On the CelebA 40-task attribute prediction benchmark, PCGrad reduces average classification error to 8.69%, outperforming the multi-objective optimization baseline by Sener and Koltun (8.95%).

On the NYUv2 multi-task benchmark, combining MTAN with PCGrad achieves superior results across 8 out of 9 evaluation metrics across semantic segmentation (20.17 mIoU), depth estimation (0.5904 absolute error), and surface normal prediction.

On Meta-World MT10, PCGrad with SAC successfully solves all 10 robotic manipulation tasks (100% success rate) while saving 2 million environment samples compared to independent SAC models, whereas vanilla multi-task SAC fails to solve half of the tasks.
On Meta-World MT50, PCGrad with SAC learns approximately 70% of the 50 manipulation tasks, matching independent training while reducing sample requirements by 15 million environment transitions.

Ablation studies confirm that altering both gradient directions and gradient magnitudes is essential because altering only gradient directions or only gradient magnitudes degrades multi-task performance substantially.
scope_and_delimitations: Evaluates gradient projection on shared network parameters in multi-task supervised learning, multi-task reinforcement learning, and goal-conditioned reinforcement learning.
Requires individual per-task gradient computations for all tasks present within each training minibatch prior to applying gradient projection.
Implements pairwise sequential gradient projections using a randomized task ordering rather than computing simultaneous multi-gradient quadratic programming solutions.
Focuses on multi-task settings where task identity metadata or task conditioning vectors are available during training.

limitations.verbatim_excerpt: A sub-optimal solution occurs when the cosine similarity between the gradients of the two tasks is exactly −1, i.e. the gradients directly conflict, leading to zero gradient after applying PCGrad. However, in practice, since we are using SGD, which is a noisy estimate of the true batch gradients, the cosine similarity between the gradients of two tasks in a minibatch is unlikely to be −1, thus avoiding this scenario. Note that, in theory, convergence may be slow if cos(φ12) hovers near −1.
limitations.summary: The theoretical convergence of PCGrad can stall or yield sub-optimal parameters if task gradients exhibit exact opposite alignment (cosine similarity of -1), which causes zero gradient updates. In addition, computing separate backward passes for every task in a minibatch introduces computational and memory overhead as the task count increases.

generalizability_gap: The authors evaluated PCGrad on computer vision image datasets and simulated robotic manipulation benchmarks; the authors did not test the algorithm on large-scale natural language processing models, real-world physical robotic platforms, generative models, or multi-agent environments.
methodological_gap: PCGrad computes task projections sequentially based on a random task order rather than solving a joint multi-task optimization problem, which introduces order-dependent variance; furthermore, computing individual backward passes for each task scales computational complexity linearly with the number of tasks in each minibatch.
future_work: Applying PCGrad to meta-learning, continual lifelong learning, multi-goal imitation learning, and natural language processing tasks.
Extending gradient surgery principles to stabilize broader machine learning settings such as two-player games and multi-agent optimization.
Designing robust and safe multi-task reinforcement learning algorithms to mitigate unsafe exploration behaviors.
Developing self-supervised and unsupervised multi-task reinforcement learning methods to overcome reward specification challenges on physical robotic systems.
